## The Retrocomputing & Film Economy Roundup

We’ve seen a surge in activity surrounding vintage hardware restoration and the shifting economics of analog photography. The most engaging discussions have centered on two distinct areas: the technical repair of 1980s workstations and the cost-benefit analysis of importing film.

In the retrocomputing sphere, the community is deeply engrossed in hardware resurrection. On Mastodon, users @dairygoatrancher and @ca_honey have shared detailed progress logs on their respective projects. @dairygoatrancher is currently recapping a Sun 3/60 workstation, highlighting the intricate installation of a ZuluSCSI drive. This involved sourcing specific components, including SN74LS652NT chips and PAL logic, while already teasing upcoming work on a Sun 4/260. Meanwhile, @ca_honey provided a mixed review of a portfolio PDA, noting that while the mainboard is pristine, the keyboard suffers from corrosion. Their post included close-up images of the battery compartment (marked "AAx3 OR LR6x3") and a circuit board featuring an Intel-compatible M80C88A chip and an Atari component. It’s a vivid reminder that the 80s and 90s tech scene is far from dead—it’s just waiting for someone with a soldering iron to bring it back to life.

On 4chan’s /fgt/ board, the economics of film are under the microscope. With local costs hitting €25.80 ($29.40) due to VAT and customs fees, users are debating the merits of importing from Fotoimpex. The conversation reveals a community of serious enthusiasts: one user is nearly done with Fujichrome and eyeing E100, while another hoards Fujifilm products. Practical shooting habits were also shared, with one user counting 42 frames using a manual winder. The thread concluded with a note on inventory availability, as Fotoimpex currently has Velvia 50 in stock, driving purchasing decisions for those waiting on specific stock.

## Technical Deep Dives: Sensors, Rust, and Strategy

Several technical threads provided valuable insights for photographers and developers alike.

Photography enthusiasts on /p/ debated the relationship between sensor size, pixel pitch, and depth of field. A key question emerged: does a Full Frame sensor with a 16um pixel pitch yield the same depth of field as a Micro Four Thirds sensor with a 4um pitch? Contributors shared links to DoF calculators to visualize blur across different setups and advised using smaller apertures to manage motion blur, simplifying image stacking for high-res panoramas. The consensus leaned toward using technical cameras to adjust the lens plane for sharpness at lower f-stops.

In the software development corner, the Rust community is discussing syntax improvements sparked by Steve Klabnik’s essay "Arguing about Arguments." User Thoth proposed shortening the `..Default::default()` boilerplate and allowing struct literals without type names in unambiguous calls. The goal is to maintain Rust’s explicit nature while reducing visual noise in the codebase.

Finally, NFL analyst Ben Baldwin released a data visualization showing the San Francisco 49ers’ league-leading pass rate on 2nd and long (8+ yards) situations, nearing 1.0. This contrasts sharply with the Seattle Seahawks, who sit at just above 0.3, highlighting the diverse offensive philosophies shaping the 2026 season.

## Quick Hits

*   **US-Canada Relations:** Reddit user @Ecstatic-Yam-3767 asked Americans if recent trade conflicts have altered their impressions of Canada, sparking a debate on bilateral sentiment.
*   **Demographic Shift:** A Bloomberg report indicates Canada’s population growth has slowed to its lowest rate since World War I, signaling potential adjustments in housing and infrastructure policy.
*   **Naval Deal:** Germany is finalizing an $8 billion deal to supply six Scorpene-class submarines to India, strengthening strategic ties between Berlin and New Delhi.
*   **Social Media Vibes:** A Bsky channel’s new PvP comment rules have been compared to Selena Gomez’s "Kiss Me Thru the Screen," with users noting heavy romantic banter between commenters.
*   **Rust Updates:** Discussions continue on syntactic sugar for default values, aiming to make struct instantiation cleaner without sacrificing clarity.

context_texts: @4529944 - /p/ — DoF — The depth of field is related to two factors: 1) the size of the circle of confusion and 2) the pixel pitch on the sensor. the bigger the CoC the smaller the DoF. the smaller the PP the smaller the DoF. So, is it safe to say, that a FF sensor with 16um PP has the same DoF as a MFT sensor with 4um PP? clusters.summary: Users on 4chan’s /p/ board are sharing original content moon photographs, with a recent highlight being a stacked image captured using an MTO-1000 telescope without a teleconverter. The photographer, impressed by the optics, noted specific settings of 1/125 shutter speed and ISO 200, while observing that PIPP software struggled with larger frames from 3x teleconverter shots. The shared image is described as a high-contrast monochrome capture featuring sharp lunar topography, including craters, maria, and highlands, under near-full moon illumination. Distinct opinions center on the quality of the glass, with one user praising the build by referring to the manufacturers as "fine piece of glass" and noting they are "commies," likely alluding to the Russian origin of the MTO optics.
